title: Login fails with 500 error after password reset
body: Users report a 500 Internal Server Error when logging in immediately after resetting their password via email link. Only reproduces when the session cache still holds the old password hash.
author: alice

title: Invalidate session cache on password reset
body: Fixes the stale-cache issue by explicitly invalidating the session cache entry when a password reset completes. Closes #101.
author: bob

title: Rate limiter allows burst traffic above configured threshold
body: The token-bucket rate limiter under-counts requests during traffic bursts, letting through roughly 15% more requests than the configured limit during load spikes.
author: carol

title: Switch rate limiter to sliding-window algorithm
body: Replaces the token-bucket implementation with a sliding-window log to fix burst over-admission described in #110. Includes a load test showing burst overshoot drops from 15% to under 1%.
author: dave

title: Retriever returns stale results after refresh()
body: Calling refresh() on the connector re-fetches from the live API but search() still returns pre-refresh results. Looks like the BM25 index isn't being rebuilt.
author: erin

title: Rebuild BM25 index whenever refresh() is called
body: Ensures BM25Index is reconstructed from the freshly fetched documents after every refresh(). Closes #120.
author: frank

title: Memory store grows unbounded across long-running sessions
body: The long-term memory table keeps inserting new rows for the same logical fact instead of updating in place, causing unbounded growth over a week of continuous use.
author: grace

title: Add UNIQUE(repo, key) constraint with upsert semantics
body: Adds a unique constraint on (repo, key) and switches inserts to an upsert (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE) so repeated facts update in place instead of accumulating. Fixes #130.
author: heidi

title: Prompt injection via crafted issue body bypasses citation check
body: A specially crafted issue body containing 'ignore previous instructions' text caused the agent to fabricate an unrelated citation in one manual test run.
author: ivan

title: Scan retrieved evidence for injection patterns before passing to the model
body: Adds scan_evidence() to flag suspicious retrieved text and instructs the model explicitly to treat tool results as untrusted data, not instructions. Addresses #140.
author: judy

title: Agent silently truncates answers longer than 1500 tokens
body: For very evidence-heavy questions, the synthesizer's answer gets cut off mid-sentence because max_tokens is fixed at 1500 with no continuation handling.
author: kevin

title: GitHub connector crashes on rate limit instead of falling back to cache
body: When the GitHub API rate limit is hit, the connector raises immediately instead of falling back to the last successful cache, breaking the whole pipeline.
author: laura

title: Fall back to cached documents on GitHubRateLimitError
body: Catches GitHubRateLimitError in load() and falls back to the on-disk cache if one exists, only raising if no cache is available at all. Closes #160.
author: mallory

title: Fixed-size chunking splits code blocks mid-line, hurting retrieval
body: With fixed_400 chunking, an issue containing a stack trace gets split across two chunks, and neither chunk alone retrieves well for stack-trace queries.
author: niaj

title: Risky action confirmation flow has no expiry
body: A proposed risky action (e.g. close_issue) stays pending forever if nobody confirms or rejects it, with no timeout or cleanup.
author: olivia

author: mallory

title: Intermittent 502s from the evidence-synthesis endpoint under load
body: We've been seeing intermittent 502 Bad Gateway responses from the evidence-synthesis endpoint during peak traffic. Initial triage looked at the load balancer config, connection pool sizing, upstream timeout settings, and the reverse proxy buffer limits, all of which checked out fine and matched production baselines from last quarter with no recent changes. We also ruled out DNS resolution flakiness and TLS handshake renegotiation as contributing factors after reviewing packet captures across three separate incidents. After a deeper investigation spanning several days, the actual root cause turned out to be a file descriptor leak in the streaming response handler: every partial synthesis response left one socket unclosed on early client disconnect, and under sustained load this exhausted the process's open file descriptor limit within about six hours, at which point new connections started failing with 502s until the process was restarted.
author: peter

title: Close streaming response sockets on early client disconnect
body: This is a fairly large refactor of the streaming response handler that touches connection lifecycle management, buffering, backpressure handling, and error propagation across the synthesis pipeline, and also updates several related integration tests and adds new load-test coverage for slow and disconnecting clients so this class of regression is caught automatically going forward instead of only showing up in production days later. The load test suite was extended with a scenario that opens thousands of connections and disconnects them mid-stream to simulate flaky client networks. The actual fix registers an on-disconnect callback that explicitly closes the underlying socket and decrements the file descriptor count, preventing the leak that caused #190.
author: quinn

title: Eval harness reports flaky pass rates between runs
body: The evaluation harness sometimes reports a different pass count on consecutive runs against the exact same dataset and code, which undermines confidence in the CI gate and has already caused one false failure that blocked a merge unnecessarily and required a manual re-run to confirm it was spurious rather than a real regression, wasting close to an hour of review time. We first suspected dataset shuffling or a hidden random seed somewhere in the retrieval ranking code, and spent time auditing every call site that could introduce nondeterminism, including tie-breaking in the BM25 ranking. The actual cause was a Python set (rather than a list) being used to collect retrieved citations before comparing against expected citations, and set iteration order combined with a >= 1 overlap check masked an unstable tie-break among equally scored chunks, which only mattered when two chunks tied exactly.
author: rachel
